text:
Rina: hey all, hi from my first day! trying to run the onboarding tutorial branch but both Buildkite and GH Actions are failing. not sure who to bug for perms. :wave:

Omar: welcome Rina! quick Q: are you seeing an auth error or a clone/build error?

Rina: Buildkite stops at cloning with: 
```
error: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
fatal: could not fetch refs
```
and then the GH Actions workflow runs but errors when trying to read secrets: "Secrets are not available to this workflow"

Leo: hmm two separate layers. Buildkite usually uses a GitHub App + deployment key to clone private repos. If the app wasn't installed for that repo, Buildkite agents get a clone failure. Can you paste the repo URL?

Rina: repo is github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-samples (private). I clicked "trigger build" from the PR page.

infra-bot: Buildkite: Pipeline "quickstart-samples/onboarding" failed to start: github app has not granted access to repository.

Omar: ok that confirms it. @leo or @ops-bot can you check the GitHub App install page? Also GH Actions secret issue may be that the workflow is using an environment with required reviewers or the repo is set to "Allow actions and reusable workflows from: only select repositories" so org secrets are blocked.

Leo: I can check. FYI sometimes the repo was created from a template and the template owner didn't include the Buildkite app. Two fixes: org owner adds the repo to the Buildkite app, or we create a deploy key on the repo and add it to the pipeline (we prefer the app though).

Rina: ty. also GH Actions shows the runner label 'self-hosted' in the workflow but our infra only has Linux self-hosted runners in the "internal" pool, not the default. could that block it?

Omar: yes if the workflow requests runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, build] and no runner matches the labels, the job will stay queued or fail. our onboarding template should default to 'ubuntu-latest' for first-run. Did you use the template or a custom workflow?

Rina: used the template. weird. maybe it got modified by the repo template owner.

ops-bot: Note: org policy "Require repository access for workflows" is enabled. Workflows from forks or PRs from first-time contributors won't have access to secrets until a maintainer enables them.

Leo: action plan: 1) I've requested Buildkite app access for quickstart-samples (should be fast). 2) Omar, can you verify the workflow permissions and runner labels? 3) Rina, for now re-run the workflow with a maintainer approval on the PR so secrets are available, or push a debug-only change that doesn't need secrets to validate cloning.

Omar: checked the repo settings: Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions is set to "Read and write" but Environments -> test-staging had protection requiring reviewers. Also the default workflow file had self-hosted label; I pushed a tiny PR that changes runs-on to ubuntu-latest for onboarding branch.

Rina: ok Buildkite app now shows pending install for the repo. re-triggered the PR build while the app is installing. Buildkite queued but now fails with LFS error: 
```
error: external filter lfs failed
fatal: smudge "git-lfs smudge -- %f" returned 128
```

Leo: that one is local git LFS config: the agent needs git-lfs installed or the pipeline should fetch without LFS for small test files. We can add a step in the pipeline to apt-get install git-lfs on linux agents.

Omar: Buildkite app install completed and permissions propagated. GH Action re-run after maintainer approval picked up secrets and job succeeded. Buildkite still failing on LFS; I've added a pipeline step to install git-lfs and requeued build.

Rina: build passed on GH Actions and Buildkite after the git-lfs fix! thanks everyone. big help getting through onboarding hiccups. :raised_hands:

Leo: welcome aboard again — we'll do a short CI orientation tomorrow to go over app installs, runner labels, and env protections. ping us if anything else blocks.
